title: R class (v11 R1-R8): recovery negative controls could pass vacuously
what_went_wrong: The NC runner chose its evidence with ls -t and treated a missing verdict as a pass; NC4 hashed in an order that made the control unfalsifiable; A28' compensated unconditionally; the preservation check re-recorded a missing pre-operation snapshot after a failure; the switches activated on any non-empty value; grant recovery did not refuse a live holder.
root_cause: The controls demonstrated that a switch changes an outcome, not that the check fails when the property is removed and passes when it is present.
detection: Astra v11 findings R1-R8, verified in the P15 task doc section 1; P15 first chain showed NC1 NOT-DISCRIMINATING (fixture hash helper out of scope), recorded separately.
impact: P11-P14 recovery evidence of 'discriminating' controls was partly unfalsifiable.

correction.applied: P15 E1-E6 (run-bound evidence, fault hook in both arms, no unconditional compensation, snapshot binding, exact-1 switches, grant-recovery refusal); P16 closed N5/N6 and observed the E1 and E4 controls.
correction.result: P15: NC 5/5, suite 39/39, unit 44/44; P16: see R5 section 28

rule: Every negative control must run the same predicate in both arms and be shown to fail the property-removed arm and pass the property-present arm on the same bytes.
